reason: ColonyVigour is a domain-owned term. The spec glossary names "colony vigour" with the values strong/fair/weak/lost as "the apiary's own reading of a colony's fitness to pollinate." It is also coarser than the vendor's six-value ColonyState: the adapter maps both queenless and swarmed to weak, and the core member lost has no vendor value mapped to it.

The keys of LIVE_BY_STATE are exactly the SDK's LeaseState values (ACTIVE, PAUSED, ENDED), and vendor text is looked up one for one inside the domain file. The spec defines "sensor cover" but gives it no states, so the lease-state distinctions are drawn by the vendor, not by the domain.

The domain glossary owns 'colony vigour' (strong/fair/weak/lost), defined as "the apiary's own reading of a colony's fitness to pollinate". The adapter also cuts the vendor's set differently: queenless and swarmed both map to weak, 'lost' has no vendor value mapped to it, and silent is not mapped.

The spec's glossary defines "metal readiness" as a domain-owned term with exactly these values ("the foundry's own reading of where the bronze is"). The set is also cut differently from DispatchState: QUEUED/POURED/ASSAYED have no mapping, 'reserved' has no vendor source, and the adapter translates only LANDED/LOADED/REJECTED into it.

LEAD_DAYS is keyed one-for-one on the SDK's PurityGrade literals (B20, B22, B23, B25) and is looked up directly with the raw lot.grade text. The domain glossary never names purity grades; it covers metal lots, readiness, notes and statuses but not grades. So these distinctions come from the vendor, not from the domain.

The spec glossary never names bronze grades or purity levels, so the domain doesn't own these distinctions; the only branch (grade === 'B20' in bell-commission.ts) tests a vendor value directly.

The spec glossary treats "vessel stage" as owned by the domain and calls it "the service's own reading" of where the vessel is relative to its berth. It is also cut differently from the vendor's VoyagePhase: DIVERTED and SCRUBBED both become abandoned, ANCHORED and BERTHING are not mapped, and approaching has no vendor value.

SIZE_FACTOR's keys are the four HullClass values unchanged, and the core looks up the vendor's text directly (SIZE_FACTOR.get(hullClass) ?? 1). The domain's text never names hull or size classes: both the glossary entry for 'pilotage fee' and the doc comment list only a base fee, a draught surcharge and a night surcharge, so these distinctions come from the vendor.

The spec glossary has a domain-owned term "hull class" whose values are PANAMAX, HANDYSIZE, FEEDER and COASTER. It defines them as the harbour master's tariff classes set in the harbour by-laws, and says the tide service just uses the same names. So the one-for-one match with the vendor comes from the domain's tariff rules, which SIZE_FACTOR applies in the pilotage fee.

HullCategory copies the SDK's four HullClass values exactly, and the use case gets them by a straight cast with no translation. The glossary never mentions hull categories, and the core only checks for PANAMAX, so the other three values exist only because the vendor defines them.

The spec glossary lists 'vessel size' (large/medium/small) as owned by the domain, described as "the harbour's own size band; a large vessel is met by a tug", and pilotage-job.ts checks for 'large' to apply that rule. The set is also coarser than the vendor's four hull classes, and FEEDER and COASTER have no mapping shown.
